newsitem.title: USA: Intel raised by reversing Merrill analyst.
newsitem.headline: Intel raised by reversing Merrill analyst.

text.p: A day after he cut his earnings forecast for Intel Corp, Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlak raised the chipmaker's estimate again on Wednesday, citing strong prospects for the Pentium MMX chip.
The earnings forecast increase helped boost Intel's stock. Shares of the world's biggest computer chip company were up two at 133 in late afternoon Nasdaq trading.
"We see a reacceleration in sequential growth in sales and earnings later this year and in 1998," Kurlak wrote in a report released Wednesday.
Kurlak raised his 1998 earnings estimate to $11.20 a share from $10.25. He also set Intel's stock price target at $200.

On Tuesday, the day after Intel released his earnings, he had reduced his 1998 earnings forcast to $10.25-$10.75 a share from $11. He said he was concerned about Intel's projection that revenue in the second quarter would rise only slightly compared with the first.
Kurlak wrote today that he believes the slowdown is because of a temporary product transition.
Earlier this year, Intel introduced the Pentium MMX microprocessor, a chip with souped-up graphics capabilities.
Since the introduction, demand for Pentium without MMX has slacked off. In addition, Intel still cannot make enough Pentium MMX chips to meet demand, Kurlak said.
"It is a mix transition issue that could have been better managed," he said. "Our concern about a possible PC demand slowdown leading to a slower 1998 is now alleviated in light of this information."
